shot.prose:
---

**1. Purpose.**
This is a daily work-dispatch dashboard showing the AI tasks currently running that require the human owner's attention, ranked by priority for the date shown.

---

**2. Most important thing first.**
The eye lands on the bold "2026-08-17" heading first — orientation, not action. What a returning reader actually came for is the first ranked task card ("layout-wave-2"), which sits below two lines of preamble text; the task list should open the page, not the date.

---

**3. Missing.**
The subtitle promises screenshots ("with the screenshots"), but no screenshot thumbnails appear anywhere in the visible area — a reader who came to review visual output finds only text cards.

---

**4. Overview vs drill-down.**
- **GLANCE:** The "ACTIVE 4" count, the orange dot + task name + timestamp on each card ("layout-wave-2 running since 6:04 PM", "day-page-ux running since 5:53 PM"), and the tag pills ("LAYOUT", "AI LOG").
- **CLICK:** "Today, ranked →" has an orange underline and arrow suggesting a link; the sidebar nav items ("Start here", "AI", "FAQ", etc.) are clearly navigation.
- **SCROLL:** At least three more active tasks are below the fold (ACTIVE 4 is stated but only 2 are on screen), and the promised five priority items are not all visible.

---

**5. Affordance.**
The two task cards ("layout-wave-2", "day-page-ux") sit inside rounded bordered boxes that strongly suggest clickability — cards almost always expand or navigate — but there is no visual cue (no chevron, no link color, no underline) confirming they are interactive. The green segmented progress bar under each card name also looks interactive (like a step-progress control) but is purely decorative status.

---

**6. Scroll regions.**
Two distinct scroll regions: the left sidebar (its own scrollbar bubble is visible at bottom-right of the sidebar panel, and "App" is cut off mid-word at the bottom) and the main content column. Two independent scrollers on a page this simple is one too many — the sidebar's separate scroll creates split-attention, and the sidebar content is short enough to not need it.

---

findings.what: Task cards look interactive (rounded bordered boxes) but carry no affordance signal — no chevron, no link underline, no hover cue — so a reader can't tell whether tapping one does anything.
findings.where: the 'layout-wave-2' and 'day-page-ux' cards in the main content area

findings.what: The subtitle explicitly promises screenshots but none appear anywhere on screen, breaking the reader's expectation set in the very first line of content.
findings.where: the 'Today, ranked → the five that need Mike, with the screenshots.' line below the date heading

findings.what: The sidebar has its own independent scroll region even though it contains only a handful of items, splitting scroll attention unnecessarily.
findings.where: the left sidebar, bottom-right scrollbar bubble near the settings gear

findings.what: The green segmented progress bar is not labeled and floats visually between the tag pill and the prose description, making its meaning (steps? health? time?) ambiguous at a glance.
findings.where: the thin green dashed line beneath the tag pills on each task card

shot.prose:
**1. Purpose.**
This is a day-level log page for 2026-08-17 that lists every AI task session run that day, each with a description, metadata tags, and an apparent dollar cost on the far right.

**2. Most important thing first.**
The eye lands on the "2026-08-17" heading, which is correct context-setting. However, the first task row — "launch-worker 2" — immediately below it demands attention before a reader can orient themselves, because there is no summary line between the title and the list to frame what follows.

**3. Missing.**
There is no day-total row — no aggregate cost, task count, or completion status — so a reader who wants to understand the day at a glance must mentally tally every row's right-hand number themselves.

**4. Overview vs drill-down.**
- **GLANCE:** The "2026-08-17" heading and the bold task-name labels ("launch-worker 2", "fire ticket v2", "experimental draft", etc.).
- **CLICK:** The left sidebar navigation items (Overview, AI, CSS, Layout, etc.) and likely the bold task names if they link to detail pages.
- **SCROLL:** All task entries from "multi-pedal" downward, including "vision-scoring", "colour-warmth", and several more below the visible fold.

**5. Affordance.**
The bold task-name text at the start of each row carries underline or colour cues suggesting it is a link, but several rows also contain similarly styled inline terms in the description body that look equally clickable without any obvious destination. The horizontal green/teal bars beneath some entries look like interactive progress bars but appear to be purely decorative cost or token meters with no label to confirm either reading.

**6. Scroll regions.**
There are two visible scroll regions: the main task-list column and the left sidebar (which has more items than its visible height). Two independent scroll areas on what is essentially a log-reader page is one too many — the sidebar content could be short enough not to need its own scroll.

findings.what: Description text under each task row is rendered at a size so small it is illegible at this viewport width, making the per-task narrative unreadable without zooming.
findings.where: the body text block beneath every task title in the main content column

findings.what: The dollar-cost figures on the far right are visually detached from their task rows with no column header or label, so a first-time reader cannot tell what the numbers represent.
findings.where: the right-most column, next to each task row

findings.what: The green/teal horizontal bars have no label or legend, leaving their meaning (token usage? progress? cost fraction?) entirely opaque.
findings.where: the coloured bars appearing below several task descriptions in the middle of the list

findings.what: No summary row exists between the page heading and the first task, so a reader cannot get a day-level snapshot (total cost, task count) without reading the whole list.
findings.where: the space between the '2026-08-17' heading and the 'launch-worker 2' first row

shot.prose:
---

**1. Purpose.**
This is a daily AI task dashboard — it shows Mike which AI jobs are actively running right now (and a count of completed ones below), ranked so he knows where to focus first.

**2. Most important thing first.**
The eye lands on the bold date "2026-08-17" — which is orientation, not action. A reader came to see what needs attention; the first active task card ("layout-wave-2" with its orange dot and progress bar) is the real entry point and should lead.

**3. Missing.**
Each card shows *status* but not *what Mike is supposed to do* — there is no explicit call-to-action or decision prompt on any card telling him whether to approve, review, unblock, or just watch.

**4. Overview vs drill-down.**
- **GLANCE:** The date, "ACTIVE 4" label, task names, orange running dots, and model tags (opus-5, fable-5) are all readable without moving.
- **CLICK:** The bold task-name headings (layout-wave-2, day-page-ux, etc.) and the pill tags (screenshot-tool, shots-history, ai-board-review, layout-system, etc.) all look like they navigate somewhere — though it is not confirmed by the image alone.
- **SCROLL:** "LANDED 52" is only partially visible at the very bottom; all 52 landed items are only reachable by scrolling.

**5. Affordance.**
The pill tags (screenshot-tool, shots-history, ai-board-review, layout-system, skills-check, vision browse — pilot run, etc.) look exactly like interactive filter chips — rounded, outlined, distinct — but whether they are links or purely decorative labels is indistinguishable. The task-name headings look like the most obvious click target but carry no underline, arrow, or other link signal.

**6. Scroll regions.**
Two separate scrolling areas are visible: the left sidebar (the Styles section is cut off at the bottom behind a gear icon) and the main content column (LANDED 52 is clipped). Two scroll regions on a narrow dashboard is one too many — the sidebar scroll competes silently with the main scroll and will confuse trackpad users.

---

findings.what: The subtitle reads as one continuous sentence but is split across two colors — orange-underlined 'Today, ranked —' and teal 'the five that need Mike, with the screenshots.' — making the first half look like a link and the second half look like a tooltip or annotation.
findings.where: the subtitle line directly below the date heading

findings.what: The progress bars for layout-wave-2 and day-page-ux show a small green sliver despite both reporting zero completed steps (0/7 and 0/6), so the visual implies progress that the text denies.
findings.where: the progress bars in the first two task cards under ACTIVE 4

findings.what: The pill tags (screenshot-tool, shots-history, vision module, etc.) are visually identical to clickable filter chips but give no signal — no hover cue, no underline, no arrow — as to whether they navigate anywhere.
findings.where: the tag clusters inside the mastermind-shots and screenshot-tool cards
